document_title: 2 to 16 polar bear dens, and FWS estimates 8

slides.headline:
10,000 runs of a model.
A middle answer of 8.
slides.body: FWS wrote its den model in R and ran it 10,000 times for AIDEA's seismic plan. It estimates 8 land-based dens in the survey area, with a 95 percent interval of 2 to 16. It is a statistical simulation, not AI.

slides.kicker: THE DEN MODEL, IN BEARS A WINTER
slides.headline:
In bears, a median of 4.
Proposed cap, 10.
slides.body: For Level B harassment the den model's 95 percent interval is 0 to 14. Level A runs 0 to 11, median 2, cap 2. The cap of 10 also covers bears away from dens.

slides.headline: 12 of 907.
slides.body: 1.32 percent of the stock. On a draft count of 819, 1.47 percent.
"We recognize the limitations of our predictive models and take estimates that significantly exceed historical data collected over decades of similar oil and gas activity on Alaska's North Slope."
labels: FWS adds that its assumptions lean toward an overestimate.

slides.headline:
Two infrared surveys,
a day apart at least.
slides.body: SnowDens, a snow model, maps where drifts build. Aircraft infrared then surveys them twice. FWS calls it four times more effective at finding dens than ground FLIR. Any putative den gets a 1.6 km exclusion zone.

slides.headline:
The proposed terms list
last winter's dates.
slides.body: The mitigation text opens the first flight November 25th. The den model opens it December 1st. The proposed terms list December 1st to 25th, 2025. Comments close December 17th.

slides.headline:
Then 12 rubber-tracked
vibroseis vehicles.
slides.body: The plan lays 37,500 wireless nodes and supports up to two 180-person camps. AIDEA's board set aside up to $175.0 million for permitting and 3D seismic work.

slides.headline:
Which end of 2 to 16
should the final
authorization plan for?

post_copy:
The proposed terms for infrared polar bear den flights over the Arctic Refuge list last winter's dates.

The first window runs December 1st to 25th, 2025. The den model in the same notice sets them this winter.

FWS wrote it in R and ran it 10,000 times for AIDEA's seismic survey.
It estimates 8 dens, with a 95 percent interval of 2 to 16.
Its median takes are 4 Level B and 2 Level A against caps of 10 and 2. The 10 also covers bears away from dens.
FWS says its estimates significantly exceed decades of North Slope data and lean toward an overestimate.
Comments close December 17th.

A coastal plain map leads, then the take medians against the caps, 12 bears of 907, FWS on its own numbers, three flight calendars and the vehicles.

Should the final terms plan for the top of the model's range or for what decades of North Slope work recorded?

#ArcticRefuge #PolarBears #NorthSlope

editor_notes_for_email: No.126 covers the FWS proposal (91 FR 73773, November 17th) for a one-year authorization of AIDEA's winter seismic survey on the Arctic Refuge Coastal Plain. Its den model, written in R and run 10,000 times, estimates 8 dens with a 95 percent interval of 2 to 16, and the proposed caps are 10 Level B and 2 Level A. It is an UPDATE of No.99 (October 29th, the Beaufort Sea rule's denning code) because this is a separate authorization for the Refuge alone, with its own model run and a comment window that closes December 17th. Three honesty locks hold on every surface: the 2025 survey dates are described only as what the proposed terms list, the cap of 10 is said to include bears away from dens (the den-only median is 4), and the model is called statistics and not AI. Session effort read medium, not the high the repo settings carry.
